subject: URGENT: Peak latency cascade -> regional swap plan & customer impact
messages:
From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@midwestretail.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@midwestretail.com
Date: 2029-04-02T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Checkout failures and 5xx spike — seeing step function at 08:50 CDT

Neha / team,

We started seeing a sharp spike in checkout latency around 08:50 CDT (US-Central) and now about 18% of requests are returning 5xx. Impact is customer-visible: abandoned checkouts, page timeouts. Peak RPS climbed from 3k to ~53k in a 2-minute window for our storefront endpoints. We're on a tight promotional window (flash sale) — this is critical.

Attached: a short capture from our synthetic monitors and the gateway logs. Can you confirm whether this is an AZ-level issue on your side or a regional routing problem? We need recommended immediate mitigation and an ETA for stabilization.

Thanks,
Alex Smith
Director of Platform Ops
Midwest Retail Co.
[Attachment: midwest-synth-0909.png]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@midwestretail.com>, ops@midwestretail.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-02T09:19:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and 5xx spike — seeing step function at 08:50 CDT

Alex — thanks for the quick alert and the captures. We're looking at telemetry now. Initial note: we see increased tail latency and a corresponding 5xx increase concentrated in us-midwest (AZ3) and a small traffic amplification on your pinned model route.

Immediate actions we're starting (short checklist):
- Routing: begin targeted cross-region spill to us-west-2 for your tenant (staged, keep 20% in region to validate)
- Serving: move your pinned model instances onto a higher-throughput profile and enable KV-prefetch for that route
- Cache: purge local prefix cache for the route then warm on us-west-2
- Comms: will provide rolling updates every 30 minutes.

Jonas, can you author the play to switch 40% if we see continued error-rate >10% for 15m? Also attaching the customer-facing note for Marissa to send if we need to escalate to executive level.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial-telemetry-snaps.zip]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-02T09:26:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures — proposed automated geo-spill play

Neha/Team,

Quick technical summary from infra: AZ3 (us-midwest-az3) has an unusual scheduler backlog on GPU hosts serving your model variant; this is causing KV-cache thrash and CPU-side queuing that manifests as 5xx and long tails. We have partial host-level IO contention logs correlated to a control-plane update at 08:43 that increased worker affinity.

Proposed immediate play (steps I'll run now):
1) Stage 20% traffic -> us-west-2 (canary) via smart-routing (TTL 30s) and observe for 5m
2) If error_rate > 10% across your routes for 10m, increase to 60% and spin up dedicated pool (via ReservedBurst) for 30m
3) If errors persist, failover DNS CNAME for your endpoint to regional-alias-usw2 (TTL 60s) and open bridge for customer-facing comms

I'll attach the routing-playbook-v2.pdf for exact commands and ETA (5–12m for the first stage).

-- Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: routing-playbook-v2.pdf]

Date: 2029-04-02T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Executive summary: Midwest Retail P1 — AZ3 scheduler backlog and mitigation steps

Team — quick executive note for situational awareness. Summary: Midwest Retail (large PLG customer, flash sale) experienced a rapid RPS spike causing scheduler contention in us-midwest AZ3 leading to 5xx/errors. Action underway: staged cross-region spill to us-west-2, dedicated burst pool if required, and cache warming. Potential customer impact: checkout failures and lost revenue; they may request credits if stabilization >30m.

Requested leadership actions:
- Approve up to 2 hours of ReservedBurst capacity on Dedicated for this tenant if Jonas recommends it (+cost acceptable for short window)
- PR/Comms support for a short executive note to Midwest leadership if we see >20% business impact

I'll stand up a 15-min briefing at :30 if any leader wants to join. Attachment: short customer-facing timeline draft.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: exec-brief-midwest-10min.docx]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@midwestretail.com>, ops@midwestretail.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-02T15:40:00-05:00
Subject: RESOLUTION: Traffic staged to us-west-2; error rate falling to baseline

Alex — final update from our side for the window:
- Timeline: staged spill started 09:28 CDT; increased to 60% at 09:36 when error rate persisted; DedicatedBurst spun at 09:40 and fully warming by 09:55.
- Result: error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.8% within 14 minutes of the 60% shift. Latency P95 reduced from 3.2s -> 310ms.
- Root cause (prelim): scheduler affinity update pushed to a subset of GPU hosts in us-midwest-az3 during increased load, creating a transient undersized worker pool for your pinned model variant. We're doing a post-mortem and will provide a timeline within 72 hours.

If you would like us to keep the warmer dedicated pool for the remainder of the promotion window, we can — we'll credit any unused minutes if not required. Apologies for the impact and thanks for your patience.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
